title: What Change Did Reformers Seek?
definition: A change intended to improve a rule, institution or condition.
imageAlt: Modern teaching cards: What Change Did Reformers Seek?. Not a reproduction of a historic document.
content:
The Propaganda Movement brought together reform advocates who used writing, speeches and public arguments to seek changes under Spanish colonial rule. In this historical name, propaganda refers to spreading ideas for a cause. It does not mean we should accept every message without checking it.

Goals included representation in the Spanish Cortes, freedom of expression and fairer treatment. The Cortes was Spain's lawmaking assembly. Representation meant having people speak for Philippine interests there. Some reformers sought the Philippines' treatment as a province of Spain with corresponding rights; that goal was different from immediately creating a separate independent country.

Recall parish reform from the earlier mission. Calls for Filipino participation in parish administration also appeared in reform demands. People did not always agree on every goal or method. A list of demands tells us what advocates wanted, not that those changes were granted.
clues: A voice
Representation meant a voice for Philippine interests in the Spanish Cortes.
Rights and participation
Advocates sought freedoms and fairer treatment, including Filipino participation in public life.
Goal versus result
Requesting a reform does not show that it was granted.
task: Which demand asks for a voice in making laws?
Representation for Philippine interests in the Spanish Cortes.
Replacing every newspaper with a private diary.
Declaring every requested change already achieved.
Treating the Cortes as a ship arriving at Cavite.
reason: Representation in the Cortes was a reform goal: a voice for Philippine interests in the Spanish lawmaking assembly. A demand is not proof of success.

title: Open the Reform Newspaper
definition: Writing made available for readers, such as a newspaper.
imageAlt: Modern teaching cards: Open the Reform Newspaper. Not a reproduction of a historic document.
content:
La Solidaridad was a newspaper associated with the Propaganda Movement. Its first issue appeared on 15 February 1889. It began in Barcelona, Spain, and was later published in Madrid. Writing in Spain allowed advocates to bring Philippine concerns to readers and officials there.

The newspaper discussed conditions and argued for reforms. NCCA's account describes demands for representation, freedoms and Filipino participation in parish and government affairs. In an essay associated with this reform writing, Rizal explained why free expression and representatives could help bring Philippine concerns to a distant government.

A newspaper can carry an argument to readers, but printing does not automatically change a law. Nor does one article prove that everyone read or agreed with it. Our modern newspaper diagram is a teaching aid, not a copy of a historical issue.
clues: Date and setting
La Solidaridad first appeared in 1889 in Spain.
Method
Publication helped carry Philippine concerns and reform arguments to readers.
Limit
Publication is a method of advocacy, not proof that a demand became law.
task: Which caption explains the newspaper's role?
La Solidaridad published Philippine concerns and arguments for reform.
La Solidaridad was a military fort in Cavite.
Every article automatically became a law in the Philippines.
The newspaper was the same organization as La Liga Filipina.
reason: La Solidaridad used publication to present Philippine concerns and reform arguments; publication alone did not grant reforms.

title: Connect People with Contributions
definition: A person who helps select, prepare and organize material for publication.
imageAlt: Modern teaching cards: Connect People with Contributions. Not a reproduction of a historic document.
content:
Three familiar names made different contributions. Graciano Lopez Jaena was the first editor of La Solidaridad. Marcelo H. del Pilar later took over its editorship. Jose Rizal contributed writing, including discussion of Philippine conditions and needed changes. They were not the only contributors.

In Filipinas dentro de cien anos, known in English as The Philippines a Century Hence, Rizal argued for a free press and Philippine representatives. Our lesson paraphrases the idea: a distant government needs ways to hear what people experience. This is an argument made by a writer, not a notice that the government had already granted those rights.

An editor and a contributor are roles, not interchangeable names for the newspaper itself. Connect a person with a documented contribution rather than assuming one person wrote every article.
clues: First editor
Graciano Lopez Jaena was the first editor of La Solidaridad.
Later editor
Marcelo H. del Pilar later became its editor.
Writer
Rizal contributed arguments for changes, including press freedom and representation.
task: Which contribution card is accurate?
Lopez Jaena was first editor, del Pilar later editor, and Rizal contributed reform writing.
Rizal alone wrote every article and was the only reform advocate.
Del Pilar founded a military arsenal instead of editing a newspaper.
Lopez Jaena was the name of the Spanish lawmaking assembly.
reason: Lopez Jaena first edited La Solidaridad, del Pilar later edited it, and Rizal contributed reform writing; their roles were distinct.

title: Discover La Liga Filipina
definition: An organized group working toward shared purposes.
imageAlt: Modern teaching cards: Discover La Liga Filipina. Not a reproduction of a historic document.
content:
On 3 July 1892, Jose Rizal founded La Liga Filipina in Manila. The NHCP marker describes aims including unity, protection against injustice, education, agriculture, commerce and studying social changes. Mutual protection means members helping protect one another.

The Liga was an association, not another name for a newspaper. Its purpose connected public concerns with organized cooperation among people. Think of the difference: a newspaper publishes an argument; an association brings people together around shared work. Both can support a reform effort in different ways.

The marker records that the association weakened after Rizal's arrest and deportation to Dapitan in July 1892. Deported means sent away by the authorities. This interruption helps explain why goals and results must be examined separately. La Liga Filipina should not be confused with the separate Katipunan.
clues: Foundation
Rizal founded La Liga Filipina in Manila on 3 July 1892.
Shared purposes
Its aims included unity, mutual protection, education, agriculture and commerce.
Interruption
The association weakened after Rizal was arrested and sent to Dapitan.
task: Which description belongs to La Liga Filipina?
An association founded by Rizal for unity, mutual protection and social improvement.
The first issue of the newspaper published in 1889.
Another name for every member of the Katipunan.
A law proving every reform goal was achieved.
reason: La Liga Filipina was an association founded in 1892 for shared improvement; it was distinct from La Solidaridad and the Katipunan.

title: Build Your Reform Field Guide
definition: Working to gain support for a cause or proposed change.
imageAlt: Modern teaching cards: Build Your Reform Field Guide. Not a reproduction of a historic document.
content:
Our museum needs a clear guide. Match the newspaper, the association and the evidence-check card with their roles. The cards are modern summaries, not original documents.

La Solidaridad shows advocacy through publication. La Liga Filipina shows organized cooperation for shared aims. A reform demand names a desired change. To establish a result, we need evidence showing what followed, such as a change in a rule or a record of an activity.

Imagine a fictional museum label: "Because a newspaper requested representation, representatives were certainly elected immediately." Repair it. The request is evidence of a goal; it does not establish that result. The contribution of reform advocacy also includes making concerns and political ideas available for discussion. Do not confuse limited success in winning demands with having no historical importance.
clues: Publish
A newspaper can present arguments and make concerns known.
Organize
An association can bring people together around shared purposes.
Check
A stated goal needs evidence of what followed before it can be called an achieved result.
task: Which explanation distinguishes method, goal and result?
Publishing and organizing are methods; a demand states a goal; a result needs evidence of what happened afterward.
Every published demand proves that the government granted it immediately.
A newspaper and an association must be the same institution.
An unfulfilled demand proves that the discussion had no importance.
reason: Publication and association are different methods. Goals state desired changes; results need evidence of what actually followed.

title: Report Your Reform Discoveries
definition: An action or idea that helps explain how events or public thinking developed.
imageAlt: Modern teaching cards: Report Your Reform Discoveries. Not a reproduction of a historic document.
content:
Connect your discoveries. Reform advocates asked for changes such as representation and freedoms. La Solidaridad carried concerns and arguments through print. Lopez Jaena, del Pilar and Rizal made different contributions. La Liga Filipina organized people around unity, mutual protection and shared improvement.

Reform advocacy and revolution are not the same method. Some demands sought changes within Spanish rule. Do not assume every advocate held one unchanging opinion, or that one newspaper alone caused all later events. Ideas, associations, policies and people's responses must be studied together.

Use this report frame: "The concern was ___. A requested reform was ___. One method was ___, used by ___. This shows ___, but it does not prove ___." The five-question mission quiz checks these lesson topics. If one is difficult, revisit its scene before targeted practice.
clues: Goals
Representation and freedoms were desired changes, not automatic results.
Contributions
Connect people with writing or editing, and distinguish newspaper from association.
Explanation
Explain the contribution and show what the evidence does not establish.
task: Which museum report fits the lesson?
Reform advocates used writing and association to seek changes; their goals and actual results must be distinguished.
La Liga Filipina was the newspaper's first issue in 1889.
All reform demands immediately became law.
One contributor alone caused every later historical event.
reason: Connect reform goals, distinct contributions and methods while checking the difference between a demand and an achieved change.
